purpose: Reviewed typed input-class specifications used to settle a-fortiori context nestings. They describe inputs, never atom-name entailments; the sweep script is their executable restatement.

the_divisor_is_not_a_whole_number.prose: A nonzero non-whole divisor in a division problem.

the_divisor_lies_between_zero_and_one.prose: The atom name grounds the open positive interval; four of five codings exclude divisor = 1, and three of those name the open interval outright (44117, 45968, 46010). Coding 45883 excludes 1 but sets no positive lower bound. Coding 46352 is the dissent: it says less than or equal to one. Under that (0,1] reading this nesting is false, because divisor 1 is narrow and is not in the not-one class.

the_divisor_is_not_one.prose: A nonzero divisor other than one. Unlike the whole-number-remainder rules under not-ten, coding 46311 counts pieces in a visual model: divisor 0.4 leaves a partial group on which the rule is genuinely defeated. Coding 45251 instead uses a long-division remainder digit and needs a whole divisor. Adding integer(D) here would make both not-a-whole-number subset not-one and (0,1) subset not-one refused_disjoint.

the_divisor_is_a_power_of_five.prose: Positive integral powers of five; the class begins at five, not 5^0.

the_divisor_is_not_ten.prose: The whole-divisor remainder input class of the two coded rules, not a name-only D != 10 class.

fraction_part_numeral_order_diverges_fro.predicate: decimal_pair(decimal(W1, Digits1), decimal(W2, Digits2)), fraction_digit_order(Digits1, Digits2, Raw), exact_decimal_order(W1, Digits1, W2, Digits2, Exact), Raw \= Exact
fraction_part_numeral_order_diverges_fro.prose: Pairs on which reading the digits after the point as whole numbers gives a different order from exact decimal value.

fraction_part_numeral_order_diverges_wit.predicate: decimal_pair(decimal(W, Digits1), decimal(W, Digits2)), fraction_digit_order(Digits1, Digits2, Raw), exact_decimal_order(W, Digits1, W, Digits2, Exact), Raw \= Exact
fraction_part_numeral_order_diverges_wit.prose: The preceding divergence class with equal integer parts, matching the integer-first rule.

numeral_length_order_inverts_decimal_val.predicate: decimal_pair(decimal(W1, Digits1), decimal(W2, Digits2)), decimal_place_count_order(Digits1, Digits2, ByLength), exact_decimal_order(W1, Digits1, W2, Digits2, ByValue), opposite_order(ByLength, ByValue)
numeral_length_order_inverts_decimal_val.prose: Pairs where more fractional places names the smaller exact decimal value.

numeral_length_order_tracks_decimal_valu.predicate: decimal_pair(decimal(_, Digits1), decimal(_, Digits2)), decimal_place_count_order(Digits1, Digits2, ByLength), exact_decimal_order(_, Digits1, _, Digits2, ByValue), ByLength = ByValue
numeral_length_order_tracks_decimal_valu.prose: Pairs where the strict fractional-place-count order agrees with exact decimal value order.

the_numerals_carry_different_place_count.predicate: decimal_pair(decimal(_, Digits1), decimal(_, Digits2)), length(Digits1, Places1), length(Digits2, Places2), Places1 =\= Places2
the_numerals_carry_different_place_count.prose: Pairs of written decimals with unequal fractional-place counts.

written_numeral_order_diverges_from_deci.prose: The loaded scale-loss automaton's divergence condition for comparing unaligned written decimal numerals.

a_factor_lies_between_zero_and_one.predicate: multiplication(decimal_factor(A), decimal_factor(B)), (0 < A, A < 1 ; 0 < B, B < 1)
a_factor_lies_between_zero_and_one.prose: Finite written-decimal multiplication inputs with at least one factor strictly between zero and one.

a_factor_is_a_non_integer_decimal.prose: Finite written-decimal multiplication inputs with at least one non-whole decimal factor.

denominator_order_inverts_for_equal_nume.predicate: fraction_pair(frac(N, D1), frac(N, D2)), D1 =\= D2
denominator_order_inverts_for_equal_nume.prose: Distinct written proper fractions with equal numerators. The denominator-order verdict is the exact inversion of fraction order throughout this class. Ground: 14 codings of order_by_denominator_magnitude, including equal/common/same/identical-numerator rows 44873, 45520, 46684, 46824, 47016, 47040, 47285 and seven unit-fraction rows. Dissent: the unit-fractions-only reading shrinks this 440-member class to N = 1 (110); it changes DEN versus CSUM to strict but changes none of the declared DEN rows. The equal-numerator majority reading, matching the atom name, is adopted.

component_sum_inverts_for_equal_numerato.predicate: fraction_pair(frac(N, D1), frac(N, D2)), D1 =\= D2
component_sum_inverts_for_equal_numerato.prose: Distinct proper-fraction pairs with equal numerators. Comparing N+D then reduces to comparing denominators and inverts fraction order. Ground: coding 46879 names equal numerators as divergence and gives a valid equal-denominator domain. Dissent: an unattested full-defeat-set reading (1,564 grid pairs) would make CSUM strictly contain CORD; it is recorded but not adopted.

component_order_inverts_for_equal_numera.predicate: fraction_pair(F1, F2), component_dominance(F1, F2, Side), exact_fraction_order(F1, F2, Exact), Side \= Exact
component_order_inverts_for_equal_numera.prose: Pairs where one fraction componentwise dominates the other at >= with at least one strict and is not strictly larger in value: the dominance rule's full 974-member defeat set. Ground: eight order_by_component_magnitude codings; rows 44707, 45650, and 47009 include equal-numerator divergence, which requires the reviewed >=-one-strict firing condition. Dissent: strict-AND yields 534 and removes every equal-numerator pair; vague row 44481 abstains. Row 46964 states equal-gap pairs as this rule's valid domain.

inverse_component_order_diverges_for_equ.predicate: fraction_pair(frac(N1, D), frac(N2, D)), N1 =\= N2
inverse_component_order_diverges_for_equ.prose: Distinct proper-fraction pairs with equal denominators, on which the smaller-components rule inverts exact order. Ground: coding 47012 names equal denominators as divergence and equal numerators as valid. Dissent: an unattested full reversed-dominance defeat-set reading is set-identical to IDEN (2,404) and would turn ICOMP subset IDEN into equality.

numerator_order_diverges_for_unequal_den.predicate: fraction_pair(frac(N1, D1), frac(N2, D2)), natural_order(N1, N2, ByNum), exact_fraction_order(N1, D1, N2, D2, Exact), ByNum \= Exact
numerator_order_diverges_for_unequal_den.prose: Pairs where total whole-number numerator order differs from exact fraction order (974 on the reviewed grid). Ground: codings 44629, 44875, and 44965 name unequal denominators as the divergence superset and equal denominators as valid; the predicate is the sound divergence-defined repair. R2 rules ties equal, grounded by the loaded gap automaton and the rows' natural-number wording. Dissent: abstain on numerator ties leaves 534 and makes the equal-numerator shipped rows disjoint.

inverse_denominator_order_diverges_for_u.predicate: fraction_pair(frac(N1, D1), frac(N2, D2)), natural_order(D2, D1, ByInvDen), exact_fraction_order(N1, D1, N2, D2, Exact), ByInvDen \= Exact
inverse_denominator_order_diverges_for_u.prose: Pairs where the smaller-denominator-is-larger verdict differs from exact order (2,404 on the reviewed grid). Ground: ten codings, 44146, 44433, 45354, 45458, 45473, 46509, 46663, 46735, 46757, and 47017, uniformly record equal numerators as valid and unequal numerators as divergence. R2 makes tie verdicts equal. Dissent: abstain on equal-denominator ties leaves 1,964 and makes ICOMP subset IDEN disjoint; GAP subset IDEN survives.

gap_order_diverges_from_fraction_order.predicate: fraction_pair(frac(N1, D1), frac(N2, D2)), D1 - N1 =:= D2 - N2
gap_order_diverges_from_fraction_order.prose: Distinct written proper-fraction pairs with equal denominator-minus-numerator gaps (440 on the reviewed grid). R1 requires the intersection for this multi-rule atom: its order rule defeats 974 pairs but its equate and proximity rules each defeat exactly the equal-gap class, so 440 is the only class that keeps all three native triples true. Coding 46920 states the class verbatim. Dissent: the order rows' broader literal or 974 divergence reading makes the two equate triples false on 534 members and is barred by closure soundness. The gap automaton is only a one-sided probe: its condition class is 974, while every 440 member carries that condition.

numerator_sum_diverges_for_unequal_denom.predicate: unavailable: coding 45599 does not fix the collection of fraction terms being summed
numerator_sum_diverges_for_unequal_denom.prose: REFUSED-UNSPECIFIABLE. Coding 45599 says: Compare the magnitude of fraction-based quantities by summing the numerators and ignoring the denominators; it calls unequal denominators divergent but does not state whether the compared inputs are two sums or a sum against one fraction. No fraction_pair predicate is sound, so all 14 ordered pairs involving this context remain refused until a second coding fixes the input shape.

the_multiplier_is_not_a_whole_number.prose: Role-marked multiplication tasks whose multiplier is not whole. Ground: rows 45157 and 46052 fix opposite operand positions while 45609 and 47257 state the multiplier role without position. Dissent: a positional reading could make B01 subset MNW sweepable, but it contradicts a coder row; all MNW cross-type pairings are refused.

the_factors_include_a_decimal_fraction.predicate: product_selection(Candidates), member(multiplication(decimal_factor(A), decimal_factor(B)), Candidates), (\+ integer(A) ; \+ integer(B))
the_factors_include_a_decimal_fraction.prose: Selection tasks containing a candidate multiplication with a non-whole decimal factor. Ground: coding 47041 asks for the largest product among a set of multiplications and names decimal fractions as divergence. It is not a single multiplication input, so all FDF pairings with B01 or NID are refused_type_mismatch.

smaller_fraction_part_numeral_names_the_.predicate: decimal_pair(decimal(W1, Digits1), decimal(W2, Digits2)), fraction_digit_order(Digits1, Digits2, Raw), Raw \= equal, exact_decimal_order(W1, Digits1, W2, Digits2, Raw)
smaller_fraction_part_numeral_names_the_.prose: Pairs where strict fraction-digit numeral order agrees with exact decimal order: the defeat class of the coded inverted rule. Ground: row 46493 says the decimal whose portion is the larger whole number is the smaller decimal. This class is the complement of FPD inside strict-raw-order pairs, so both SFN pairings are refused_disjoint.

the_tenths_digit_is_nine.prose: One-place written decimals with tenths digit 9. The increment-the-fraction-numeral rule crosses a place boundary and is defeated. Ground: row 47062 gives tenths less than 9 as valid and tenths equal to 9 as divergence. Dissent: allowing any length with a tenths 9 is unsound (3.95 to 3.96 succeeds); the one-place reading is required.

the_numeral_carries_a_nonzero_fraction_p.prose: Written decimals with a nonzero fraction part. Ground: row 47296 has a student subtract the decimal part from the whole part to determine one decimal's value; that subtraction is the student's move, not an input operand structure. Dissent: treating it as a subtraction operand would make T9 subset NNF refused_type_mismatch.

the_subtrahend_carries_a_nonzero_fractio.predicate: subtraction(minuend(M), subtrahend(decimal(SW, SD))), integer(M), SD \= [], \+ all_zero(SD)
the_subtrahend_carries_a_nonzero_fractio.prose: Whole-number-minus-decimal subtraction problems whose subtrahend has a nonzero fraction part. Ground: row 44544 specifies a genuine two-operand input. Its pairings with T9 and NNF are refused_type_mismatch.
